blocks.text: with the message that she ought to say, "اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ (As Salaamu Alaykum). May I come in?"[^1]

Hadhrat Aslam reports, "Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s instructions to me were, 'O Aslam! Stand guard at my door but never accept anything from anyone.' When he one day saw me wearing new clothing, he enquired where I had gotten it from. '(Your son) Ubaydullaah bin Umar (RA) gave it to me,' I replied. To this, he said, 'You may take from Ubaydullaah but from no one else.' Standing at the door one day, Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) came and asked permission to enter. When I told him that the Ameerul Mu'mineen was busy at that moment, he lifted his hand and hit me so hard behind my head that I let out a scream. I then went in to Hadhrat Umar (RA) who asked me what the matter was. I informed him that Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) had hit me and narrated the entire episode to him. 'By Allaah!' Hadhrat Umar (RA) exclaimed, 'I shall see to Zubayr. Send him in.'
When I let Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) in, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, 'Why did you hit the slave?' Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) replied by saying, 'He was going to prevent us from seeing you.' 'Has he ever before refused you permission to enter my door?' Hadhrat Umar (RA) enquired. When Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) replied in the negative, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, 'Then when he tells you to be patient because the Ameerul Mu'mineen is busy at the moment, then do so and excuse me. By Allaah! When an animal is mauled (by one), all the other animals eat him up (if you start hitting him, so will others).'"[^2]

Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once sought permission to see him at a time when his head happened to be in the hands of his slave girl who was busy combing his hair. He granted Hadhrat Umar (RA) permission to enter and then quickly pulled his head away from her. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Leave her to comb your hair." Hadhrat Zaid (RA) said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Had you sent for me, I would have come to you." Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s reply was, "It was I who is in need (and I shall therefore have to come to you)."[^3]

Another narration states that when some people requested permission to see Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) after the Fajr salaah, he allowed them in. He then veiled his wife with a shawl saying, "I did not want to keep you waiting (any longer by taking more time in sending her out)."[^4]

Hadhrat Moosa bin Talha (RA) says, "I once went with my father to my mother. When he entered the room and I followed him in, he struck me so forcefully on the chest that I fell on my buttocks. He then said, 'Do you enter without permission?!'"[^5]
Hadhrat Muslim bin Nadheer narrates that a man was already peeping in (the house) when he asked Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) permission to enter. Hadhrat
Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.51).
